grade.reason: The agent patch makes the same functional change as the merged patch. The backend now accepts `reason` instead of `msg`, so `setattr(response, "reason", ...)` is equivalent to the upstream explicit assignment. The frontend now dispatches `{ response: { reason } }`. The existing test was updated the same way. The only difference is that the upstream adds an extra http_version test and a changelog entry, which don't affect behavior.

result:
Editing a response's reason phrase in the web UI now updates the flow. I haven't run any tests or the frontend, as you asked.

The frontend sent `{ response: { msg } }`, but `Response` has no `msg` attribute. The `PUT` handler in `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` accepted `msg` and did `setattr(response, "msg", ...)`, which set a stray attribute and left `reason` unchanged. I changed three places:

- **Frontend:** `web/src/js/components/FlowView/HttpMessages.tsx` now sends `{ response: { reason } }`.
- **Backend:** `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` now accepts `reason` (alongside `http_version`) instead of `msg` when updating a response.
- **Test:** `test/mitmproxy/tools/web/test_app.py` now sends `"reason": "Non-Authorisé"` and asserts `f.response.reason`. The old assertion on `f.response.msg` passed only because of the stray attribute.

The backend no longer accepts `msg` for responses, so any external API client that sent it will now get a 400 (unknown update key) instead of a silent no-op.
